Featured case study

Chaotic Birthday
Visual System

A controlled maximalist card concept built from a reusable visual grammar.

Brief & audience

Create a birthday card concept for a close friend who appreciates playful, visually loud humor. The work is a self-directed portfolio study, not a client commission.

Emotional job

Make the recipient feel vividly celebrated while leaving clear space for a personal message.

Research signal

The research scan suggested tactile texture and surreal playfulness. I translated that direction into watercolor blooms, risograph color and restrained digital interference.

Diagnosis → revised prompt

The initial generation spread attention across too many objects and left no reliable message area.

“Surreal tiered cake as the single oversized organic focal form; botanical watercolor, fluorescent risograph and digital glitch collage; pink, acid green, cobalt and cream; confine misregistration to edges; reserve the upper-left quarter as message-safe space; avoid embedded text and polished vector finish.”

This excerpt summarizes the structured prompt rules shown below. The revision constrains composition and materials while preserving the celebratory energy.

Compare the refinement

Drag the handle to reveal how the focal hierarchy changed.

JSON system

Stable rules specify palette, materials, focal hierarchy and text-safe space. Occasion, relationship, emotion and focal subject remain variable.

Inspect the JSON framework ↗

Variation test & outcome

Two further Glitch Garden occasions test whether the same grammar survives a change in message. In this self-evaluated portfolio test, the final birthday composition has clearer hierarchy and usable message space; no commercial outcome is claimed.

01 / Research translation

Signals in.
Style systems out.

This is directional research, not invented user testing. I triangulated current visual forecasts, marketplace language and greeting-card behavior—then translated recurring signals into testable art-direction rules.

01 · CREATIVE FORECAST

Tactile feeling beats sterile polish

Adobe’s 2026 themes emphasize sensory texture, emotional connection and playful surrealism. Translation: paper grain, visible repair, imperfect edges and one emotionally legible gesture.

Adobe Creative Trends ↗
02 · VISUAL DISCOVERY

Curated individuality is replacing sameness

Pinterest’s 2026 forecast points to poetcore, cool blue, alien/celestial cues, glitchy glamour and refined maximalism. Translation: familiar references combined through an owned visual grammar.

Pinterest Predicts 2026 ↗
03 · MARKETPLACE LANGUAGE

Humor is specific, sassy and relationship-aware

Current Etsy discovery language repeatedly frames Gen Z cards as funny, sassy and meme-aware. Translation: build the joke from a relationship truth, not a disposable internet reference.

Etsy market scan ↗
04 · CATEGORY BEHAVIOR

The card must make someone feel seen

Greeting-card reporting emphasizes authenticity and increasingly acknowledges heavier life moments. Hallmark also reports that physical cards make recipients feel more special than email or text. Translation: emotion first, aesthetic second.

Hallmark category evidence ↗
DESIGN HYPOTHESIS

For this portfolio, “Gen Z native” means emotionally direct, visually tactile, culturally current and self-aware—never simply louder, younger or meme-filled.

02 / HeartStamp concepts

Four feelings.
Zero greeting-card cringe.

Each concept begins with the emotional job—not an aesthetic keyword. The style follows the relationship, occasion and tone.

System controls

Stable: palette, material rules and one focal hierarchy. Variables: occasion, relationship, primary and secondary emotion, focal subject. Negative constraints: generic stock illustration, illegible embedded text, artist imitation. Evaluation: message-safe space, clarity and emotional fit.

03 / Style range

One brief.
Many visual dialects.

Range matters only when intent survives the style change. Every study reserves usable message space and retains a clear emotional focal point.

Style range criteria

Each study tests whether the emotional focal point and message-safe area remain legible as materials, lighting and visual language change.

04 / Original style systems

Not a one-off look.
A reusable visual grammar.

Prompt architecture

Stable rules live with each named style system below. Occasion, relationship and emotion are variable fields in the JSON framework. Exclusions and evaluation criteria are documented in the featured case and scorecard.

A

Glitch Garden Letters

Botanical watercolor × fluorescent risograph × digital interference. Built for celebration, admiration and lovable chaos.

  • One oversized organic focal form
  • Misregistration stays at the edges
  • 30% quiet space protects the message
  • No polished vector perfection
B

Tender Brutalism

Architectural certainty × vulnerable pencil marks. Designed for the emotions people struggle to phrase.

  • Hard geometry holds soft characters
  • One repaired or imperfect object
  • Emotion is restrained, never cute
  • Paper texture keeps it human
C

Cosmic Scrapbook

Analog ephemera × Y2K fragments × gentle aliencore. A system for distance, memory and chosen family.

  • Two worlds joined by one visual thread
  • Personal objects replace generic icons
  • Depth through torn-paper layering
  • Interface fragments stay unreadable

05 / Controlled variation test

Same DNA.
Different emotional jobs.

Two new occasions per system test whether the visual language can travel without collapsing into a single image. Palette, material logic and composition rules remain stable; subject and emotion change.

A

Glitch Garden Letters

Stable: watercolor blooms, fluorescent halftone, edge glitches, quiet message space.

B

Tender Brutalism

Stable: hard sheltering geometry, soft paper characters, one repaired or imperfect object.

C

Cosmic Scrapbook

Stable: separate worlds, one luminous connection, personal ephemera and unreadable interface fragments.

How the consistency study was scored

Self-evaluated controlled consistency study. Each variation was visually checked for palette consistency, material logic, message-safe space, emotional differentiation and focal clarity. These are portfolio judgments, not external validation or completed audience testing.

3/3palette retained
3/3material logic retained
6/6message-safe compositions

06 / Iteration

Better prompts begin with better diagnosis.

I evaluate hierarchy, emotional accuracy, typography space, palette discipline and batch repeatability—then change one variable group at a time.

BEFORE · GENERIC & CROWDED
→
AFTER · CONTROLLED MAXIMALISM

Case 01 — Composition repair

Problem: every object competed; no space remained for a message.

Correction: one hero silhouette, constrained palette, upper-left safe zone and texture hierarchy.

Result: still chaotic in feeling, now usable as a card system.

BEFORE · EMOTIONALLY UNCLEAR
→
AFTER · ONE HONEST GESTURE

Case 02 — Emotional focus

Problem: familiar apology symbols produced visual noise, not sincerity.

Correction: replace the symbol pile with one hesitant character and one repaired object.

Result: the image communicates vulnerability before any copy is added.

07 / Structured prompting

Creative direction,
stored as data.

The schema separates stable style DNA from variable occasion, relationship and emotion fields—making controlled batch generation possible.

heartstamp_style_prompt.json
{
  "occasion": "chaotic_birthday",
  "relationship": "close_friend",
  "emotion": {
    "primary": "joy",
    "secondary": "playful_chaos",
    "intensity": 9
  },
  "style_system": {
    "name": "Glitch Garden Letters",
    "influences": [
      "botanical watercolor",
      "fluorescent risograph",
      "digital glitch collage"
    ],
    "palette": ["#FF4F9A", "#D7FF3F", "#192180", "#FFF4DC"],
    "stable_rules": [
      "one oversized organic focal form",
      "misregistration limited to edges",
      "minimum 30 percent message-safe space"
    ]
  },
  "composition": {
    "aspect_ratio": "4:5",
    "focal_subject": "surreal tiered cake",
    "text_safe_area": "upper-left quarter"
  },
  "avoid": [
    "generic stock illustration",
    "corporate polish",
    "illegible embedded text",
    "artist imitation"
  ]
}
